title: Training Questions on the Outage Credit Minimum Duration for Energy-Assisted Electric Service Agreements
content:
These training questions cover the minimum duration an outage record must reach for the sustained-outage credit on an **Electric Service Agreement** that has received payments from an energy assistance agency.

> **Rule.** The minimum duration for the sustained-outage credit is half (0.5 times) of the schedule's minimum outage credit duration when the agreement received two or more payments from an energy assistance agency in the 12 calendar months before the credit is posted, three quarters (0.75 times) of that minimum when it received exactly one such payment, and the schedule's minimum outage credit duration when it received none.

**Which payments count?**
Payments posted to the agreement from an energy assistance agency. Payments through any other channel are not part of this count.

**Over what period?**
The 12 calendar months before the credit is posted. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. A hypothetical payment dated on the boundary day, exactly 12 whole calendar months before the posting date, is outside the count; one dated the day after the boundary day is inside it.

**What does the minimum duration govern?**
Two things. The record qualifies only when its qualifying duration is at least this minimum duration, and the excess hours used for the increments are measured from this same minimum duration.

**What happens with no such payment?**
No reduction applies.

**A hypothetical case.** Take a schedule minimum outage credit duration of 20 hours and a record with a qualifying duration of 16 hours.

| Energy assistance agency payments in the period | Minimum duration | 16-hour record |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | 10 hours | qualifies; excess 6 hours |
| exactly 1 | 15 hours | qualifies; excess 1 hour |
| none | 20 hours, no reduction | does not reach the minimum |
